title: IRIS-GNN: Leveraging Graph Neural Networks for Scheduling on Truly Heterogeneous Runtime Systems
problem: Heterogeneous accelerator systems require managing vendor-specific toolchains and code fragmentation across different accelerators, and even with IRIS abstraction, optimal dynamic scheduling still requires manual user input to understand task graph structures.
motivation: Automating scheduling policy selection through learned task graph analysis can eliminate manual optimization while maintaining performance portability across heterogeneous systems from smartphones to supercomputers.
method: IRIS-GNN uses a machine learning system called a Graph Neural Network (which learns patterns in how tasks connect to each other) to automatically analyze incoming work. The system classifies each task graph into one of three types: ones where keeping data near the processor matters most, ones where running tasks in parallel matters most, or a mix of both. Based on this classification, it automatically selects the best scheduling strategy—the runtime method for assigning work to different accelerators—from IRIS's options.
key_novelty: It applies Graph Neural Networks for the first time to automatically classify task structures and select the right scheduling strategy for systems with different types of accelerators.
contributions: IRIS-GNN hybrid scheduling policy combining GNN-based task graph classification with IRIS dynamic policies
Graph Neural Network model for classifying task graphs into locality, concurrency, and mixed categories
Comprehensive performance evaluation of IRIS-GNN against IRIS's complete spectrum of dynamic policies
Analysis of GNN inference overhead and real-world application scenarios
limitations: Paper does not discuss limitations of the approach in the abstract.
primary_theme: GNN-based scheduling for heterogeneous accelerator systems
